correctness.rationale: Endpoint differentiation is exact. The real DFT symmetry and Parseval decompose the (2m-2)-dimensional tangent into 2x2 complex paired blocks and, when m is even, a real unpaired block. Their Gram eigenvalues are computed exactly; the singular-value multiplicities sum correctly, the lower value is positive in the open duty interval, and analytic remainder plus inverse function theorem establishes sharp local stability. Independent Jacobian construction checks 45 configurations, including the Nyquist and half-duty cases; finite tests are not used as the general proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic research searches and primary comparisons found no exact result giving the full constrained real Fourier-moment Jacobian spectrum and its half-duty isometry for regular m-arc masks. Courtney 2010 covers qualitative order-m recovery, Batenkov et al. asymptotic complex Fourier matrix conditioning, Jiang 2026 low-mode oscillation bounds; none mathematically entails the two explicit spectral values, multiplicities, or duty-fraction optimizer. The risk of a prior unindexed elementary calculation remains.

value.rationale: The precise low-frequency conditioning of endpoint recovery is a natural invariant in reconstruction of multiple arcs. An exact two-level real spectrum uniformly for all m and alpha, a sharply optimal unique half-duty local isometry, and an explicit divergence at thin arc limits provide genuinely quantitative structure not supplied by generic recovery or spectral bounds. No arbitrary slice or unsupported global extension is claimed.
